p.i: te[?] extirpastis. Magna quidem Pastorum vestrorum, in primis autem magni illius Caluini vigilantia id factum esse, nemo quantumuis inuidus diffiteri potest: sed tamen in eo non parua certè laus vestra est, quod sanis Pastorum vestrorum consiliis paruistis, neque aduersariorum iudicia veriti, neque potentissimorum regum inuidiam & minas pertimescentes. Itaque in ea, quam nobis Dominus verbo suo patefecit, veritatē purissima constanter & intrepidè permansi-stis. Neque non tamen in vestra hac ciuitate Satā sua flabella, & pessimorum errorum dis-seminatores habuit, sed summo Dei benefi-cio nunquā isti quicquam inter vos obtinere & efficere potuerunt. Vicit enim veritas, & statim extincta sunt ea veneni semina, quæ pater ille mendacij serere inter vos conaba-tur. Quod sigillatim etiam commemorare me non pigebit. Nam cùm anno Domini M.D. XXXV. salutarē illud Euangelij lumen tota ciuitas vestra diuino potius miraculo, quàm humana vlla industria lubenter am-plexa esset, quàm variè vos teterrimus ille humani generis hostis per suos emissarios sit aggressus, satis constat. Neque vero de iis tantùm loquor, qui vos à iam recepta cælesti doctrina, callido quodam artificio & blandis verborum

page.notes: The scan shows no paragraph indent, so the whole page is one paragraph continuing from the previous page. Doubtful readings: "te[?]" before "extirpastis" (a sign after "te" I could not identify). The wavy sign after "esse" (printed "effe" with a mark) is read as plain "esse"; it may be a flourish or an abbreviation. The "extincta sunt" join is hard to read. "verborum" at the lower right is a catchword. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout; the s forms could be confused with f in this italic type. The running head is the word EPISTOLA, with a full stop printed after it.
